name: Crown of the Earth
summary: At Aldrassil, Tenaron Stormgrip asks young night elves to draw sacred water before they leave Shadowglen. The rite recalls Mount Hyjal and the immortality their people gave up there.

sections.title: A Lesson in Recent History
sections.body: Before young night elves leave Shadowglen, their elders teach them what their people lost. At the Battle of Mount Hyjal, the kaldorei sacrificed the World Tree Nordrassil to defeat Archimonde and banish the Burning Legion. The blast cost them their ageless immortality and sacred shield. Tenaron Stormgrip teaches this history as he gives novices a rite, preparing them with humility and purpose for a changing world.

sections.title: Waters of the Well
sections.body: To complete the rite, you draw water from the moonwell north of Aldrassil with a crystal phial. Moonwell waters carry remnants of the ancient Well of Eternity. Druids channel their restorative power into the wild, while Sentinels honor the wells as tranquil shrines to Elune. The kaldorei remain wary: arcane sorcery is forbidden, and the wellspring that sustains their land recalls the reckless magic that nearly broke the world.

aliases: who gives crown of the earth
faq.answer: Tenaron Stormgrip is a night elf high in the upper boughs of Aldrassil in Shadowglen. He mentors young night elves nearing the end of basic training, giving them rites that teach their people's solemn history before they travel onward into Teldrassil.

faq.q: What is the purpose of collecting moonwell water?
faq.answer: Filling the crystal phial begins a journey that is both practical and ceremonial. Moonwell waters hold ancient magic that druids use to nourish the land, and the rite teaches young kaldorei their society's sacred obligations.

faq.q: Why did the night elves lose their immortality?
faq.answer: During the Third War, the night elves unleashed the ancestral power woven into the World Tree Nordrassil to destroy Archimonde atop Mount Hyjal. The sacrifice destroyed the Legion's vanguard, but cost the night elves their eternal youth and immunity to disease.

Moonwells hold diluted essences linked to the Well of Eternity. Druids and priestesses channel their energies for healing, blessing, and communion with nature, while the kaldorei forbid arcane sorcery because of the catastrophes reckless magic caused in ancient history.

faq.q: Where does this quest chain lead next?
aliases: what comes after crown of the earth
faq.answer: Returning the filled phial completes the opening lesson in the Crown of the Earth series. Tenaron sends you to Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar, who has you fill phials at other moonwells across Teldrassil for the druids of Darnassus and, in the end, Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm.

faq.q: Where is the moonwell for this quest located?
faq.answer: The moonwell lies a short walk north of Aldrassil's great boughs, among the woods of Shadowglen.

angles.text: As a night elf, this rite marks your passage out of Shadowglen. It ties your path to the sacrifice atop Mount Hyjal and your duty to safeguard Teldrassil.
As a druid, you know moonwells as essential tools of the Cenarion circle, offering purified conduits of nature's energy to tend the forest's balance.
As a priest, you honor Elune at moonwells, reflective shrines where the waters are consecrated beneath the Mother Moon's gaze.
